draft.title: Political constraints
card: A political constraint is a limit on policy that comes from politics, not from economics. Governments want to win elections, so they weigh votes as well as economic advice.
A policy can be sound for the economy but unpopular with voters. Examples are cutting government spending, raising taxes or reducing a benefit.
A government may delay, water down or avoid such a policy. This is more likely when an election is near.
The result can be a policy that is weaker or later than the economy needs, or one that favours popular choices. Governments can still choose unpopular policies, especially early in a term.
draft.remember: Governments weigh votes as well as economic advice, so sound but unpopular policy may be delayed or softened.

a.q: What is a political constraint on economic policy?
opts: A limit on policy because voters may dislike a choice
A limit on policy because the policy takes time to work
A limit on policy because of events in other countries
A limit on policy because the central bank is independent
a.why: A political constraint comes from the need to keep voter support. Delays in effects and world events are different limits, because they do not come from voters. Neither is a political constraint.
a.clue: Think about what a government needs in order to stay in office.

b.q: Economists advise a state government to cut spending to reduce a budget deficit. The election is four months away. Which response best shows a political constraint?
opts: It postpones the cuts until after the election
It cuts spending after the cuts take a year to show
It cuts spending because world interest rates have risen
It cuts spending because its advisers have agreed
b.why: Postponing the cuts to protect votes is a political constraint, since the choice is shaped by the election. The other options are driven by time, world events or agreement, not by voter reaction. A government that cuts spending anyway is not shown to be constrained.
b.clue: Which choice is shaped by the coming vote?

a.best: A limit on policy because voters may dislike a choice

b.best: It postpones the cuts until after the election

problems.detail: The option 'It cuts spending after the cuts take a year to show' is muddled: it is unclear whether the government cuts after a year or the cuts take a year to have an effect. Rewording it, for example 'It cuts spending, knowing the effects will take a year to show', would make the time-lag distractor clear.
Why (a) explains the time-lag and world-events distractors but never says why the central bank independence option is wrong.
